Svelte runs a `$:` statement at most once per microtask. When the statement assigns one of its own inputs after an `await`, in a `.then()` callback, after `tick()`, or in `setTimeout`, `setInterval` or `queueMicrotask`, the assignment lands in a later microtask and runs the statement again, possibly forever. The rule also follows calls into functions that the statement calls, and then reports the call as well. It looks at components that are not in runes mode.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/infinite-reactive-loop": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  import { tick } from "svelte";
  let count = 0;
  $: if (count) tick().then(() => {
    count = 0;
  });
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  let count = 0;
  $: if (count > 10) {
    count = 0;
  }
</script>
```
